content: Long-term memory agent systems (Mem0, Letta/MemGPT, Zep/Graphiti, Supermemory) converge on: never let the LLM adjudicate which fact is current; use deterministic timestamp/recency-based supersession instead, and mark old facts as invalidated rather than deleting them (temporal annotation) so history stays queryable. Even so, published benchmarks show these frameworks resolve conflicting/stale memories only 7-28% of the time, i.e. this is an unsolved problem industry-wide, not a solved pattern to just adopt.
